originalTitle: Australia news live: PM urged to restrict violent pornography after teen’s death; Labor working on release of Oscar Jenkins
content: Defence minister to meet tech industry Richard Marles, the defence minister, is headed to the US and UK this week for talks with technology companies and partners in Washington and Westminster. Marles’ trip coincides with commemorations in Australia and the United States to mark the 75th anniversary of the Anzus Treaty. He will meet members of the Trump administration to talk about the Aukus nuclear deal, as well as US military rotations to Australia. The trip will also include meetings on AI, including with tech company Anthropic. The government signed a memorandum of understanding with the company in April. The assistant minister for science, technology and the digital economy, Andrew Charlton, will also attend the San Francisco leg of the trip, part of efforts to woo Anthropic to invest in Australia. In London, Marles will meet with the new secretary of state for defence, Wes Streeting. “On the 75th anniversary of the ANZUS Treaty between Australia and the US we celebrate the enduring foundation of trust, cooperation, and shared purpose that underpins our Alliance today,” Marles said. The NSW opposition leader, Kellie Sloane, says she has written to Anthony Albanese after a 16-year-old girl died from a suspected sexual strangulation incident. Sloane said the reports were shocking and had “rocked everyone to their core”, saying she had written to the prime minister about the need to tackle violent pornography. I’m saying, you know, after the shock of the last week, that let’s act now, let’s not wait any longer. The opposition leader said certain types of pornography should be placed into the most restricted category and pressure should be applied on porn companies and social media giants to “just make sure wherever we’re at, we can block it”. It has the ability to program the young, vulnerable minds of a generation of people whose first sexual experiences are being distorted because of this. Kids at 16, this is shocking. And it’s becoming normalised. Sloane went on to say education about consent was also a critical prong, even if it’s a “very tough” conversation between parents and teenagers. It’s a hard conversation to have with your kids. But around consent, we need to model that behaviour as well. Sloane added that she told Albanese the NSW Liberals were “very supportive” of Chanel Contos’ campaign, Fix Our Feeds, which urges an opt-in mechanism for algorithms. These algorithms prey on people, whether it’s young boys feeding them increasingly misogynistic content online, whether it’s girls preying on their vulnerabilities about their looks and their self-worth. McCarthy calls Mundine a ‘trailblazer’ for Indigenous Australians in sport NT senator Malarndirri McCarthy paid tribute to Mundine this morning, calling him a “a trailblazer for Indigenous Australians in sport”. He was a proud father, grandfather and mentor whose legacy will live on through the generations he inspired, both in and out of the ring. My thoughts are with the Mundine family, as well as all those who knew and loved Tony. Some Nepal flood victims had minutes of notice. Others had seconds Guardian Australia’s Cait Kelly has a dispatch from the recovery effort in Kathmandu, Nepal. She writes: On Sunday the combined toll in Nepal and Tibet climbed to 781 dead and more than 3,000 people missing. Forty-three of them are Australians. The humanitarian crisis on the ground is huge – but aid, a large amount of it from Australia, has started to arrive. An additional $3m, on top of $5m already announced, was confirmed on Monday morning. The army barracks have become the heartbeat of the crisis – bringing survivors in, taking supplies out and trying to place the dead with their families, so they can be laid properly to rest. “With every helicopter there are mixed feelings,” says Plan International’s Unni Krishnan, who is on the ground in the Nuwkot district to oversee the response. “It’s a scene of hope and despair – there are families here who have been waiting for three days to hear about their loved ones … Some of them will arrive and some of them will not.” Read more here: Warning: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander readers are advised that this post contains images and names of Indigenous Australians who have died. Australian boxing great Tony Mundine dies aged 75 Indigenous Australian boxing great Tony Mundine has died, aged 75. AAP reports the father of former boxer and NRL star Anthony Mundine had a heart attack on Sunday. Born in Baryulgil, near Grafton in northern New South Wales, Tony Mundine was the first Australian to fight in four different weight divisions, challenging for the world middleweight title against Argentina’s Carlos Monzón in 1974, in a bout stopped in the seventh round. Mundine leaves a significant boxing legacy. Anthony was an IBO middleweight and WBA super-middleweight world champion, whose son Rahim won his fourth career fight from as many professional bouts on the Gold Coast only last week. We think that there are real privacy risks with people having photos of themselves, images of themselves taken by these glasses without their consent and when they don’t even know it’s happening … However, Watt says some people were using smart glasses for reading and other accessibility reasons. I think we’re really quick to demonise something like this because it seems out of hand, like it’s dodgy or somehow it could be used for the worst. You’re playing catchup.
